taxpayer.filing_status_claimed: none (no return filed); SFR used married filing separately; petitioner asserted he was divorced (single)
taxpayer.notes: Nonfiler; decided on respondent's unopposed motion for summary judgment. Divorce decree dated Dec. 30, 2012 accepted as true.

adjustments: gross income $254,512 from third-party reports (wages $213,630; capital gain $32,227; MSA taxable payments $6,236; retirement distribution $2,417; dividends $2)
standard deduction $12,000; taxable income $242,512; tax $60,569 at married-filing-separately rates
sec. 72(t) additional tax $242; total tax $60,811; withholding credits $42,961; net underpayment $17,850
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Petition disputed only that a return was filed in Sept. 2022 and the married-filing-separately status (he was divorced)
conceded: Income adjustments deemed conceded (no assignment of error, Rule 34(b)(1)(G))
Respondent did not dispute petitioner's divorce decree dated Dec. 30, 2012

findings_of_fact.fact: Third-party reports showed 2018 gross income $254,512: wages $213,630, capital gain $32,227, MSA payments $6,236, retirement distribution $2,417, dividends $2
findings_of_fact.snippet: capital gain of $32,227, taxable payments of $6,236 from a medical savings account, a taxable distribution of $2,417

findings_of_fact.fact: Standard deduction $12,000; taxable income $242,512; tax $60,569 at married-filing-separately rates
findings_of_fact.snippet: Allowing a standard deduction of $12,000, the IRS determined taxable income of $242,512, generating tax of $60,569

findings_of_fact.fact: Sec. 72(t) additional tax $242; total tax $60,811; withholding $42,961; net underpayment $17,850
findings_of_fact.snippet: calculated with reference to petitioner’s net underpayment of $17,850.

findings_of_fact.fact: No contention that petitioner was 59 1/2 or older when the $2,417 was distributed, nor any other exception
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner has advance d no contention that he was age 59 1/2 or older when the $2,417 was distributed to him.

findings_of_fact.fact: IRS prepared SFR on September 12, 2022 with sec. 6020(b) certification; petitioner never filed a 2018 return
findings_of_fact.snippet: On September 12, 2022, the IRS prepared a substitute for return (SFR) setting forth the adjustments discussed above.

findings_of_fact.fact: No facts alleged showing reasonable cause for failure to pay
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner has alleged no facts and produced no evidence showing that his failure was “due to reasonable cause and not due to willful neglect.”

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner divorced by decree dated Dec. 30, 2012 (unmarried in 2018)
findings_of_fact.snippet: “I have a D ivorce Decree dated Dec. 30, 2012.”

issues.question: Did petitioner receive 2018 gross income of $254,512 as determined from third-party reports?
issues.holding: Yes; petitioner raised no dispute and is deemed to have conceded the income adjustments
issues.computable_reason: Sum of reported income items; uncontested

issues.question: Is petitioner liable for the 10% additional tax under sec. 72(t) on the $2,417 retirement distribution?
issues.computable_reason: 10% of $2,417, rounded; no age or other exception claimed

issues.question: Is petitioner liable for the sec. 6651(a)(2) failure-to-pay addition where he filed no return but the IRS prepared a sec. 6020(b) SFR?
issues.holding: Yes; SFR is treated as the return for sec. 6651(a)(2); addition of $3,659 computed on $17,850 net underpayment sustained; no reasonable cause shown
issues.computable_reason: SFR satisfies 6651(g)(2) as a return; no reasonable cause alleged; amount is 0.5%/month of net underpayment up to 25%

issues.question: Does using married-filing-separately rates instead of single rates change petitioner's 2018 tax?
issues.holding: No; harmless error: for petitioner's income bracket in 2018 the single and married-filing-separately rates are the same, producing the same liability
issues.computable_reason: Compare 2018 single vs MFS rate schedules (and $12,000 standard deduction) at taxable income $242,512

decision.text: An appropriate order and decision will be entered for respondent.
decision.summary: Summary judgment for respondent: $60,811 deficiency, $242 sec. 72(t) tax, and 6651(a)(1), 6651(a)(2) ($3,659) and 6654 additions sustained; MFS vs single status harmless

notes: Unopposed motion for summary judgment; amounts rounded to nearest dollar by court. Small tax case designation removed because deficiency exceeded $50,000. The $60,811 deficiency includes the $242 sec. 72(t) tax. 6651(a)(1) and 6654 additions deemed conceded (not assigned error).
